sections.heading: Paradip Refinery: Indian Oil's Petrochemical Gateway on the Odisha Coast
paragraphs: Paradip's process industry is built around Indian Oil's Paradip Refinery in Jagatsinghpur district, the corporation's eleventh refinery. It was commissioned in 2016 and dedicated to the nation on 7 February 2016, with a capacity of 15 million tonnes a year processed through a single atmospheric column, the first of its kind for Indian Oil. Crude arrives by very large crude carriers at three single point moorings about 25 km out to sea, and the refinery is designed to run entirely on high-sulphur crude.

The site has been moving steadily from fuels into petrochemicals. Indian Oil lists a polypropylene unit producing several PP grades, and an ethylene recovery unit feeding a mono-ethylene glycol plant that makes MEG, DEG and TEG from FCC off-gases. In July 2020 the Indian Oil board approved an integrated paraxylene and PTA complex at Paradip at an estimated Rs 13,805 crore, sized at 800,000 tonnes a year of PX and 1.2 million tonnes of PTA, with 50,000 tonnes of toluene. Indian Oil's refinery page still lists the PX and PTA plants as under implementation.

sections.heading: Paradip Port: 18 Berths and 218 Oil Tanks Around the Harbour
paragraphs: The refinery exists because of the port. Paradip's foundation stone was laid on 3 January 1962 at the confluence of the Mahanadi and the Bay of Bengal, the first vessel berthed on 12 March 1966, and on 18 April 1966 it was declared the eighth major port of India and the first on the east coast commissioned after independence. The Paradip Port Authority now lists 18 berths, three single point moorings and a Ro-Ro jetty, an approach channel 18.7 m deep, and vessels of up to 300 m length overall.

The port describes the surrounding industrial area as a large oil and liquid bulk ecosystem, with about 218 oil storage tanks run by oil companies and terminals, handling crude and petroleum products through berths, pipelines and refineries. Its expansion programme targets a capacity of 289 million tonnes a year. For a supplier of stainless tube, this means Paradip's buyers are refinery and petrochemical units, tank farms and terminals, and the contractors who build and maintain them, rather than the pharmaceutical plants found in most of our other markets.

sections.heading: Where Electropolished 316L Tube Earns Its Place in a Paradip Petrochemical Unit
paragraphs: Bulk refinery piping is carbon and low-alloy steel, so electropolished stainless is a small-bore, high-value item here. The services that call for it are analyser sample lines and sample conditioning panels, impulse lines to pressure and flow transmitters, and chemical injection and dosing lines on units such as the alkylation unit, the sulphuric acid regeneration unit, the hydrogen generation unit and the glycol plant. In these lines a rough or contaminated bore adsorbs and releases trace sulphur, moisture and hydrocarbon, and the analyser reads the tube instead of the stream.

Electropolishing removes the cold-worked skin left by tube drawing, lowers the Ra of the bore and leaves a chromium-enriched passive film, so there is less surface for contaminants to hang up on and better resistance to pitting in the salt air of a coastal site. For sample and impulse lines we supply ASTM A269 seamless tube in 316L, and for sour, acidic or chloride-bearing streams, 904L supplied electropolished. ASTM A312 pipe in 304L and 316L covers the larger stainless utility runs. If an MEG, PX or PTA package specifies polished product lines, SF4 316L sanitary tube to ASTM A270 is available for those too.

sections.heading: Test Certificates and PMI for Paradip Contractors
paragraphs: Expansion and turnaround work at a refinery is released to site through main contractors and third-party inspectors, and no tube is installed without complete paperwork. Each heat we supply carries an EN 10204 3.1 certificate traced to its heat number, with chemical analysis from a NABL-accredited laboratory. Every length is checked by PMI before it leaves, which matters on a site where 304L, 316L and 904L lengths may lie in the same storage yard.

Each electropolished lot comes with our internal Ra report so the inspector can match the finish to the line list, and our quality system is certified to ISO 9001:2015. If the inspection test plan for your Paradip package calls for extra witness points or a specific marking format on each length, send it with the enquiry and the quotation will reflect it.

sections.heading: Sending a Paradip RFQ
paragraphs: A complete enquiry gets a quotation within 24 hours. For refinery, petrochemical, tank-farm or port-terminal work at Paradip, include:
bullets: The unit or package the tube is for (refinery analyser shelter, MEG or PP plant, PX-PTA, tank farm, jetty pipeline) and whether you are the plant, an EPC contractor or an instrument panel builder.
Grade and finish per line: 316L or 904L electropolished instrument tube for sample and impulse lines, SF4 316L where a package specifies a polished product line, SF1 304L or 316L for utilities.
Size, wall thickness, length and quantity, with the standard: ASTM A269 or A270 tube, A249 welded tube, A312 pipe.
Your inspection test plan or third-party inspection agency, and the delivery point at the Paradip site.

sections.heading: Supplying Paradip and Coastal Odisha
paragraphs: Electropolished pipes and tubes for Paradip are dispatched from our Mumbai base at Shop No. 05, 113/117, Dr. MG Mahimtura Marg, 3rd Kumbharwada, Mumbai 400004, with end caps fitted and the heat number marked on every length. Each quotation states the dispatch date and transit to your site in writing.
